text.content:
Baator is a system of nine worlds orbiting a sickly red giant. It is sinister but rigidly ordered: an absolute hierarchy rules, discipline exists to break dissenters, and the locals endlessly scheme for advancement. The ambitious find great opportunity here, but failure is final. Compared with the Wheel's worst places it can feel almost comfortable.

Physics behave normally and ships pass safely, but heavy traffic from across the Wheel means captains must obey local traffic control exactly. Violators face Baator's armies rather than a mere fine, although a sufficient bribe can usually buy their indifference.

Baator draws unsavory visitors, and its natives have a long tradition of dangerous sorcery. Advancement depends on daemon pacts, which test both summoning skill and the ability to negotiate a profitable, survivable bargain. The most powerful figures are practically immortal, bound up in layered contracts that have stripped away much of their humanity. Mutation and corruption are widespread. Wildlife is scarce, having been exhausted in pursuit of power, and what remains is mostly mutated former humans.

Avernus, nearest the sun, is a waterless red-hazed wasteland where seeping gas ignites into deadly fireballs; depraved @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceHalfling0]{Halfling} miners in Draukari cut superb gems, and the @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceTiefling0]{Tiefling} ruler Bel may train Chaos armies there. Dis is a world-city of black iron and the usual destination for visitors, who need passes for everything and mostly stay in the Port Quarter, while Dispater rules from the Iron Tower. Minauros is an acid swamp under lead-melting heat whose capital is sinking; its ruler Mammon is a thirty-meter serpent-bodied figure of boundless greed.

Phlegethos is entering a periodic volcanic upheaval that also renews its rich minerals; Lady Fierna nominally rules, but her father Lord Belial holds the reins. Stygia is a frozen, storm-lashed sea of floating forests and ice-floe cities, fractured into city states since its ruler was sealed in an iceberg. Gas giant Malebolge exports gas and the bone of huge dead space whales under Glasya, said to be Asmodeus's daughter. Maladomini is a ravaged ruin where the mad @UUID[Compendium.dtd40k.races.Item.dtdRaceAasimar00]{Aasimar} Triel keeps rebuilding his capital. Cania makes elite plasma weapons under the sorcerer Mephistopheles. Nessus, guarded by an armada, hides Asmodeus in its deepest trench.

Story Master only: adventure seeds for this sphere.

Prince Levistus of Stygia, freed only one day a year from his icy prison, offers nearly anything for his release, which may first require killing a Daemon. After a failed attempt on Glasya's life, the system is under martial law, and the heroes are hired, seemingly by Asmodeus, to find the assassin before paranoia sparks open war.

An unnatural warp storm is choking traffic into the sphere and may be an enemy attack. A desperate father asks the heroes to retrieve his child, lured to Baator by promises of luxury; rumor says a powerful Baatorian is gathering such recruits as a mass sacrifice, though it may just be tourism promotion.
